terms.sub: Characteristics of Benign and Malignant Neoplasms
clues: Literally translates as 'to form backward' and serves as a hallmark of malignancy.
Associated with nuclear hyperchromasia, giant tumour cells, and tripolar or bizarre mitoses.
Lack of cellular differentiation in a neoplasm, with marked variation in cell size and shape.

terms.sub: Characteristics of Benign and Malignant Neoplasms
clues: Spread occurs via lymphatic channels, blood vessels, or direct seeding of body cavities.
Never occurs in benign neoplasms regardless of their size or growth rate.
Discontinuous spread of malignant tumour cells from a primary site to distant secondary organs.

terms.sub: Characteristics of Benign and Malignant Neoplasms
clues: Mediated by paracrine fibrogenic factors such as TGF-beta secreted by tumour cells.

Examples include RAS, MYC, ERBB2, and CCND1.
Gain-of-function mutations convert a single allele into a dominant cancer-driving gene.

terms.sub: Molecular Basis of Cancer: Tumour Suppressor Genes
clues: Located on chromosome 17p13.1 and mutated in more than half of all human cancers.
Induces p21 for G1 arrest, GADD45 for DNA repair, and BAX for apoptosis.
The master tumour suppressor gene known as the guardian of the genome.
Provides the metabolic basis for visualizing tumours with 18F-FDG PET imaging.
Generates metabolic intermediates required for rapid nucleotide and lipid biosynthesis.
Preferential uptake of glucose and conversion to lactate via glycolysis by cancer cells even when oxygen is abundant.
Produced by Aspergillus flavus contaminating improperly stored maize and groundnuts.
Induces a signature G-to-T transversion at codon 249 of the TP53 gene.
A potent hepatocarcinogenic mycotoxin that synergizes with hepatitis B virus to cause hepatocellular carcinoma.

terms.sub: Clinical Aspects, Grading, Staging, and Paraneoplastic Syndromes
clues: Examples include Cushing syndrome and SIADH in small cell lung carcinoma.
May be the earliest clinical presentation of an occult neoplasm.
Symptom complexes in cancer patients that cannot be explained by local tumour mass, invasion, metastasis, or hormones native to the tissue of origin.

terms.sub: Clinical Aspects, Grading, Staging, and Paraneoplastic Syndromes
clues: Mediated largely by tumour necrosis factor (TNF), IL-1, IL-6, and proteolysis-inducing factors.
